references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew's Sermon on the Mount where Jesus says exactly the same thing: "Ask, and you will receive. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives, and he who seeks finds, and to him who knocks it will be opened."
Jesus teaches that everything asked for in faith will be received – a promise of answered prayer that underscores the same principle of asking and receiving.
Jesus says that whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and you will receive it – a parallel promise of answered prayer.
Jesus promises that whatever you ask in his name, he will do it – a promise that whoever asks will receive.
Jesus says that if you remain in him and his words remain in you, you may ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.
Jesus encourages the disciples to ask the Father in his name and promises that they will receive, so that their joy may be complete.
God promises through the prophet Jeremiah that when his people call on him and pray to him, he will hear them, and when they seek him with all their heart, they will find him.
John writes that whatever we ask, we receive from him, because we keep his commands and do what pleases him – a confirmation of the promise of answered prayer.
John writes that we have confidence before God that if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us, and we know that we have received what we asked of him.
James encourages anyone who lacks wisdom to ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault – a promise that whoever asks in faith will receive.
Wisdom says: "I love those who love me, and those who seek me will find me" – an Old Testament foundation for the promise that whoever seeks will find.
David testifies that he sought the Lord, and the Lord answered him – an experience illustrating the principle that whoever seeks and asks is heard.
